checks.check: 3. Diff-panel semantics (fraction of encoded panel pixels > 20)
checks.detail:
r2 is sparse dim speckle, not pure black. The whole panel has 1.9-4.2% of pixels above 20, and the mouth box has 14.6-27.5%. The r2 maximum is 89, about 40+8x6. Around the mouth, r5 is denser than r2 and sparser than r3 and r4 in all 8 lineage frames.

Mouth-box share above 20 (bmsb f1/16/120/221; bw f1/60/140/184):
- r2: 24.8/24.8/22.0/23.6; 17.1/14.6/20.0/18.5
- r5: 48.7/38.5/46.2/51.7; 36.4/26.6/43.9/37.4
- r4: 52.1/60.0/60.7/58.8; 40.9/38.3/51.2/53.2
- r3: 87.3/88.4/82.4/88.5; 65.9/65.7/78.2/75.4

The whole panel follows the same order; the closest case is bmsb f221, where r5 is 8.4% and r4 is 9.1%. The focus set gives the same r2 < r5 ordering: mouth box 15.8-27.5% vs 28.0-54.4%. The lossless still panels agree too. Nonzero share for bmsb f16 is r2 5.1, r3 17.8, r4 10.0, r5 7.1%; for bw f140 it is 4.2, 13.0, 9.0, 7.4%.

checks.check: 4. Stills PNGs lossless relative to the canvas
checks.detail:
Every stills PNG is exactly 2H x W. Three tests show the PNGs are lossless.

(a) In the PNG, the BEFORE vs r2 full-frame cells differ by exactly 0 outside the face box, in all 8 stills frames. All nonzero pixels are inside the face box: 1.35-2.04% of the cell, max 2-5 LSB. The same comparison on the mp4 frames shows 55-77% of pixels nonzero outside the face box, max 9-12 LSB, which is pure codec noise.

(b) Every diff-panel value in the PNG lies on the 0 / 40+8k lattice: 4-24 distinct values. The one exception is 90, the right-hand column divider that my crop included. The mp4 panels have 70-170 off-lattice values.

(c) The PNG vs mp4 full-frame cells differ by a mean of about 2 LSB, p99 5-7, max 13-33, which is codec noise.

Caveat: by Laplacian variance the PNG is not sharper. It is equal to or slightly lower than the mp4 (for example 119.9 vs 124.2), because codec noise adds high-frequency energy. 'Lossless' holds, but 'visibly sharper' is not supported.

checks.check: 5. Honest native-resolution comparison (focus set)
checks.detail:
At native 512 px, full frame and 3.0-3.1x zoom, I cannot tell BEFORE, r2 and r5 apart in any viewed frame (bmsb 1/16/120/221, bw 1/60/140/184). The mouth shape, teeth, lip colour and chin all look the same. Lossless true differences vs BEFORE, full-frame cell:
- r2: max 2-5 LSB, 1.4-2.0% of pixels changed, 0-17 px above 2 LSB.
- r5: max 4-18 LSB, 2.3-4.2% changed, 46-675 px above 2 LSB, 0-4 px above 10 LSB. The worst case is bmsb f221 at 18 LSB, which is the video's most-different frame.
In the zoom row, r5's true difference (mean 0.25-0.43, p99 2-3 LSB) is smaller than the encoded column-to-column codec noise (mean ~1, p99 4-5, max 20-31), so only the diff row can show r5's changes. In that row, r5's changes follow the lip contours and teeth outlines plus an arc along the jaw/chin line; for bmsb it also covers the beard (f221 is the densest). r2 is diffuse low-level speckle with a faint jaw arc (bw f140).

visual_observations:
BEFORE, r2 and r5 look the same to the eye in both sets, in the full frame and in the mouth zoom, across all 16 viewed frames. Examples are bmsb frame 16 (widest mouth) and frame 221, and bw frames 184 and 140. Only the diff row separates them: r2 is faint scattered colour speckle, while r5 is somewhat denser, with bright traces along the lip line, teeth edges and the jaw/chin contour. In the 5-column set, r3 is clearly the densest (most of the face lights up) and r4 is between r5 and r3.

One real quality point is shown correctly: black_man_short_beard r5 fails the calibrated landmark bar by a small margin (0.104 / 0.36 against 0.10 / 0.35), so its verdict line is orange. black_woman r5 passes it (green). The landmark line's colour follows only the calibrated verdict, so a line that reads 'strict: FAIL | calibrated: PASS' is green. That matches the stated design, but the legend does not say it.

Text is legible at both widths. The title stays clear of the dividers, the frame counter sits at the top right without overlap, and the r4 and BEFORE descriptions wrap cleanly onto two lines.

problems.description: black_woman r2 prints 'jaw+lip landmarks 0.050 / p99 0.14 px' next to 'landmark gate strict: FAIL'. The true mean is 0.05021, just above the 0.05 limit, but at 3 decimals a viewer sees 0.050 <= 0.05 and a FAIL, which looks contradictory. This appears in both sets.
problems.suggested_fix: Print the landmark mean and p99 to 4 decimals (0.0502 / 0.144), or add the margin when the value is within rounding of the threshold.

problems.description: The zoom-row caption 'differences under ~1 LSB here are video-codec noise' understates the codec noise. I measured the gap between encoded columns where the true raw difference is at most 2-5 LSB (r2 vs BEFORE): mean ~1 LSB, p99 4-5 LSB, max 11-14 LSB. r5's true zoom difference (p99 2-3 LSB) is below that noise, so any difference a viewer thinks they see in the zoom or full-frame rows is codec noise, not the model.
problems.suggested_fix: Reword the caption to something like 'column-to-column differences up to ~5 LSB here are codec noise; r5's real changes are smaller, see the diff row'. Or rely on the lossless stills for that claim.

problems.description: The expectation that the PNG is visibly sharper than the mp4 is not supported by measurement. By Laplacian variance the PNG is equal to or slightly lower than the mp4 (codec noise adds high-frequency energy), and the two differ by only about 2 LSB on average at crf 10/12. The PNGs are lossless, proven by exact zeros outside the face and on-lattice diff values, but not noticeably sharper.
problems.suggested_fix: In any README or user-facing text, call the stills 'lossless (exact pixel values)' rather than 'sharper'.

checks.check: BEFORE 252.0 vs r5 400.7 measured under comparable conditions
checks.detail: The runs were back to back: 23:36:27-23:39:07 and 23:39:18-23:41:40. They share the same harness sha (181f7439…), torch 2.5.1 / numpy 1.23.5 / opencv 4.9.0, GPU, env file, 6 streams with the same identities, and min_timed 60 s; all repeats ran at least 60 s. GPU busy fraction is 0.9992 in both, so both are GPU-bound. SM clock median is 2610-2625 MHz for BEFORE vs 2460-2475 for r5, so r5 ran slower clocks and was not advantaged. Power 209 vs 204-206 W; temperature 65-67 C in both. mem_available minimum 8.6-8.9 vs 9.3-9.5 GB. Non-harness CPU load 0.58-0.59 vs 0.59-0.62 cores on a 32-core host. The run differences come from the backends themselves: pack 8 vs 16 (bs8 shipping engine vs bs16), and loops 12 vs 18 to reach 60 s. Caveats: one pair in one order only. Each pair result reproduces an independent earlier run within 0.2 fps (Ta_baseline 251.8 at 06:44; T_srcg50 400.9 at 22:51). Both pair runs logged stop_warning 'worker N exited (exitcode None)' with status complete. The same warning appears in most earlier runs; I did not investigate it.

checks.check: r5 >= 400 fps is robust
checks.detail: It is marginal. The four r5 repeats are 401.81, 400.05 (T_srcg50) and 401.38, 400.08 (T_srcg50_pair). All four are at or above 400, but only by 0.05 to 1.81 fps; the smallest margin is 0.01%. The spread between repeats (1.3-1.8 fps) is bigger than the smallest margin. In all 7 runs I checked, repeat 2 is lower than repeat 1, with an SM clock median about 15 MHz lower, so throughput sustained beyond about 2 minutes is probably about 400.0-400.1. Runs longer than 65 s were not measured, so I cannot say whether it stays at 400 or above. Plainly: r5 sits at 400, not comfortably above it.

visual_observations: I viewed frame 100 of lineage_all_rounds/black_man_short_beard, the focus_before_r2_r5/black_woman still (frame 184) and label, zoom, diff and metric crops. Labels are legible. r5 is yellow and marked NEW, and each fps line carries the 'Nx BEFORE' speedup. Full-frame and zoom columns look indistinguishable by eye. The zoom crops sit at the same position in every column. In the diff row, r2 shows faint sparse speckle. r3 has clearly the most, a bright mouth/teeth outline. r4 is moderate. r5 shows sparse speckle on the lips, teeth and beard/jaw edge, more than r2 and less than r4. The verdict lines render green or orange as coded. For r5 black_woman the line 'landmark gate strict: FAIL | calibrated: PASS' is green. The mp4 is not a reliable view of r5-vs-BEFORE differences in the zoom and full-frame rows. The codec error against the lossless canvas is 2.3 LSB mean and 6 LSB at p99 in the zoom row, the same for every column. So in the mp4, r2-vs-BEFORE reads 0.86-1.23 MAD against a true 0.14-0.15, and r5-vs-BEFORE reads 1.05-1.29 against a true 0.27-0.50. The diff row and the lossless stills are where real differences show. The focus README's claim that r5's changes are 'visible only in the diff row' is a perceptual judgement I cannot fully verify. It holds for the mp4, where they are below codec noise. Individual pixels differ by up to 8-24 LSB in the lossless data.

problems.description: The verdict colour follows the proposed, report-only calibrated landmark bar, not the repo's strict gate. The quality JSONs record chin.landmark_dev_mean_px / p99 as 'fail' and the calibrated bar as 'report'. Yet the line 'landmark gate strict: FAIL | calibrated: PASS' is drawn green. r5 is green on 4/6 identities while failing the strict gate on 6/6; r2 is green on 5/6 with strict passing 2/6. problems.description: In the 400 px set (lineage_all_rounds) the diff panel downsizes the 426-478 px face crop to 400 px with INTER_NEAREST, so 12-30% of source pixels are never drawn on 5/6 identities: 84.2%, 76.9%, 85.7%, 70.0% and 88.2% shown; south_asian 100%. That contradicts 'any change shows' in the video and 'shows exactly what reaches the viewer' in the README. It affects all columns equally, and the 512 px focus set shows 100%.
problems.suggested_fix: Max-pool before downscaling, e.g. cv2.resize(cv2.dilate(diff, 2x2 kernel), ..., INTER_NEAREST) or a block max, so no changed pixel is dropped. Or state that the 400 px diff is subsampled and point readers to the focus set.

problems.description: The 40 + 8x floor is stated, and it applies identically to all rounds (same function, 'per round' in the caption). Nothing says it exaggerates: an imperceptible 1 LSB change is drawn at 48/255, and anything of 27 LSB or more saturates to 255. r3's max of 63 and r4's max of 34 therefore look the same as 27. A viewer may read r5's speckle as a visible change.
problems.suggested_fix: Add a caption such as: '1 LSB (invisible in the output) draws as 48/255; >= 27 LSB saturates; same mapping in every round column'.

problems.description: The in-video caption 'differences under ~1 LSB here are video-codec noise' understates the codec noise. Measured against the lossless canvas: 2.3 LSB MAD and 6 LSB p99 in the zoom row, about 2.0 MAD in the full frame, equal across columns. In the mp4, r5's true zoom difference from BEFORE (0.27-0.50 MAD) is buried under about 1 LSB of codec-induced difference between columns.
problems.suggested_fix: Reword to 'codec noise here is ~2 LSB mean / ~6 LSB p99; use the diff row, the metrics or the lossless stills for pixel-level comparison'.

problems.description: r5 >= 400 fps is marginal and the READMEs present 400.9 in bold with no margin note. Per repeat: 401.81, 400.05, 401.38, 400.08, so the smallest margin is 0.05 fps. The second repeat is lower in every run, and sustained throughput was not measured.
problems.suggested_fix: In both READMEs state: '400.05-401.81 per repeat (4 repeats, 2 runs); >= 400 by 0.05-1.8 fps; second repeats consistently lower; longer runs not measured.'

problems.description: The lip-following zoom adds viewport motion. There is no misalignment between columns (verified), but the crop moves in integer source-pixel steps on 62-80% of frame transitions, up to 3-5 px, or about 7-18 display px. Against a fixed crop, this raises the frame-to-frame second difference of rigid features (subnasale, upper lip) by about 5-25%. Temporal-smoothness judgements in the zoom row therefore include crop motion, identically for all columns.
problems.suggested_fix: Use a sub-pixel crop (cv2.getRectSubPix or warpAffine) with heavier or zero-phase smoothing. Or note in the README that the zoom viewport moves and that temporal flicker should be judged from the metrics or the full-frame row.

visual_observations:
What a viewer sees at native resolution (focus set):

- **East frames** (f14 = r5's most-different frame, f183 = widest mouth, plus f203 and f1/60/120/240): in the full-frame and 3.5x zoom rows, BEFORE, r2 and r5 look identical to me. Teeth shapes, the lip-corner darkness, the goatee, the moustache/philtrum and the skin all match.

The differences show up only in the diff row.
- **r2** is faint, sparse dim speckle over the lower face, with a barely visible lip-line.
- **r5** is visibly denser speckle and a brighter lip-seam outline. It also has a patch of grey-white speckle in the grey beard along the jaw (middle f10, around landmark 152, y≈460-500).

Numbers from the lossless stills (full frame vs BEFORE):

| | Changed pixels (share of frame) | Max diff | Share of changes that are 1 LSB | PSNR in lip box |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r2 | 1.5-3.1% | 2-5 LSB | ~99% | 54.3-55.5 dB |
| r5 | 2.0-5.3% | 5-15 LSB | 85-96% | 45.5-52.0 dB |

- The 15 LSB maximum is in the beard texture at the jaw (x 295, y 481), not on the lips.
- Nothing changes outside the face box in either round.
- The honest takeaway: r5 is measurably further from BEFORE than r2, but the difference cannot be seen in the picture itself.

Something present equally in all three columns, i.e. inherited from BEFORE:
- The generated mouth area is soft and blurry.
- In middle_eastern_man_full_beard, the soul patch below the lower lip renders as a blurry dark square, and the beard inside the generated region is smeared compared with the sharp beard on the jaw edge (see f10 and f16 zooms).

So r5 neither fixes nor worsens this. The README already notes that the facial-hair identities were rated 'needs improvement' in BEFORE.

problems.description: The r3 row in the top-level README is wrong on three ranges, and it contradicts the lineage README in the same folder. It says 'aperture delta 0.28-0.33 px'; the correct range is 0.234–0.368. It says 'landmarks ... / 0.65-0.98 px'; p99 is actually 0.649–1.012. It says 'lip corr 0.997-0.998'; the correct range is 0.9969–0.9986. Source: quality_metrics/runs/*__srcv1_taesdtrt.json, 6 identities. These JSONs are dated 18:38–18:40, before the r3 README (18:46), so the r3 README copied numbers that were already wrong. The r3 README also gives mouth flicker 1.017–1.021; the correct range is 1.017–1.025.

problems.description: §8.1 says 'against 24.12 ms for srcmix FP16' and the §8.5 table says 'srcmix FP16 | 24.2'. The per-block JSONs give 22.13 ms for srcmix down1–up2 in blocks/blkA_thr_8e-06.json (3.08+2.98+0.24+0.48+1.28+6.81+7.27) and 22.19 ms in blocks/gmac_sets.json. The implied saving is therefore about 6.8 ms, not 8.8 ms. The 24.1 figure also contradicts the README's own arithmetic, since the srcmix UNet sum is 36.87–37.02 ms. Also, srcmix is not all-FP16: its down3/mid blocks (0.72 ms of the sum) are INT8.
problems.suggested_fix: Replace 24.12 with 22.13 in §8.1 and 24.2 with 22.19 in §8.5, and relabel the row 'srcmix (FP16 except INT8 down3/mid)'.

problems.description: The lineage README says the diff row is 'the pixel-level authority' and that it shows 'black where identical ... so even a 1 LSB change stays visible'. That is not true for lineage_all_rounds. For 5 of 6 identities the face+neck box is 426–478 px, and it is nearest-neighbour downscaled into a 400 px cell, so whole rows and columns of source pixels are never drawn. I recovered the full-resolution diff map from the focus stills (which are upscaled, so nothing is lost there) and found that 11–30% of changed pixels are missing from the lineage panels. Example: middle_eastern r5 still 1 hides 5,800 of 19,324 changed pixels; black_woman r2 hides 1,493 of 6,209. south_asian_woman (392 px box) and all focus videos are unaffected. Sparse differences such as r2's are the ones most likely to vanish.
problems.suggested_fix: Make the diff cell at least as large as the face box, or downscale with a max-filter (dilate by ceil(s/CW), then take the maximum per block) so that any changed pixel stays lit. Or state that the diff row in the 400 px lineage set is subsampled and point readers to focus_before_r2_r5 for the pixel-level diff.

problems.description: The claim that r5's change is at the ±1 LSB noise level is misleading. It appears in the r5 README ('about as large as ±1 LSB of random noise ... mouth PSNR 51–53 dB vs 51.5–51.9'), the top README ('mouth PSNR at the ±1 LSB noise level'), the focus README and §8.5. It holds only for the per-frame mean mouth PSNR. Against the iid ±1 LSB arm, r5 is clearly larger on every other statistic: worst-frame mouth PSNR 43.1–47.0 vs 51.4–51.6 dB; face max abs 14–28 vs 3–9 LSB; aperture delta 0.084–0.141 vs 0.044–0.073 px (about 2x); landmark p99 0.20–0.47 vs 0.13–0.33 px; calibrated bar 4/6 vs 6/6. Source: runs/*__srcg50.json and *__synthetic_faces_noise1lsb_raw.json.
problems.suggested_fix: Qualify the claim as 'mean mouth PSNR is at the ±1 LSB noise level; worst frames are 4–8 dB below it, and aperture and landmark changes are about 1.5–2x noise'.

problems.description: 'One encode for all, so every column is equally faithful ... (within 0.02 dB)' is not supported. No file records a 0.02 dB figure. I compared mp4 frames with the lossless stills (2 frames per identity) and got a per-column RGB PSNR spread of 0.08–0.20 dB in the full-frame row and up to 0.56 dB in the zoom row. Away from the column dividers (16 px inset) the spread is 0.016–0.075 dB for lineage and 0.001–0.032 dB for focus, and up to 0.16 dB in the zoom row. The outer columns (BEFORE and the last one) come out about 0.1–0.2 dB more faithful than the middle columns, which include r2 in the focus set. This is still much smaller than the 0.56–1.22 dB bias of the old A/B videos.
problems.suggested_fix: Write 'within ~0.2 dB (≤0.08 dB away from the column dividers), measured on the stills' or record a measurement to back the claim.

problems.description: 'Differences below ~1 LSB in the full-frame and zoom rows are H.264 noise' understates the codec floor. Against the lossless stills, the encode error in those rows is 2.06–2.23 LSB RMS in luma, 2.35–2.64 LSB RMS in RGB, with a luma p99 of about 5 LSB (PSNR about 39.5–41 dB) at both crf 12 and crf 10.
problems.suggested_fix: Say that differences of up to about 5 LSB in those rows can be codec noise, and point to the diff row and metrics.

problems.description: Some §8 and r5 wording is imprecise. (a) §8.4 'Why: ... up2.upsamplers.0.conv ... is now INT8; ~18 small layers go back to FP16' describes gmac_0.59 (1 layer added, 18 removed vs blkA8). r5's gmac_0.50 does not quantize up2.upsamplers.0.conv and is a strict subset of blkA8 (29 layers removed, none added). problems.suggested_fix: Say explicitly that the §8.4 'Why' refers to gmac_0.59. Write '117 INT8 layers in total (99 beyond r2)'. Write 'tied lowest'. Remove the r5 folder from the video list or add its videos.
